sections.overview: Lethrinus crocineus Smith, 1959 is an emperor fish of the western Indian Ocean, recorded from East Africa and nearby islands east to Sri Lanka.
sections.identification: It is tan to grey, often with dark scale bases and reddish or yellowish fin margins; the South African species account reports a maximum length of about 55 cm.
sections.habitat: It occurs on reefs and nearby sandy grounds, including deeper reefs, and is reported to about 150 m in the western Indian Ocean.
sections.diet: Published accounts describe a fish-and-crustacean diet; one regional linefish review says the details remain little known.
sections.behavior: FishBase describes it as solitary in coastal trawling grounds and coral-reef areas.
sections.reproduction: The species accounts consulted do not establish a spawning season for this emperor.
sections.ecology: Older accounts sometimes treated it as Lethrinus mahsena, but the FAO catalogue distinguishes the two by consistent scale-count differences.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists a 2018 IUCN assessment of Least Concern; this is a dated assessment, not a measure of present local abundance.
